report:
Finding: Model B is more biased toward web news/blog/article style content and formatting than Model A.

Why I think this:
- Logit-lens tokens cluster heavily around news/blog domains:
  - People/roles typical of newswire: “Obama,” “billionaire,” “politicians,” “journalists,” “spokeswoman,” “chairman,” “metropolitan.”
  - Blog/media/platform tokens dominate positions 2–4 across many late layers: “blogs,” “blogger,” “blog,” “photo,” “video,” “film,” “facebook,” “http,” “sexy.”
  - Site/section/ad/metadata tokens at early positions: “ad,” “ads,” “Mail,” months (“May,” “Mar”), “TV,” “Radio,” “Live.”
  - Section-like words: “Sports,” “Traffic,” “Fashion.”
- Strong formatting bias in the top layers: very high-norm cells at layers 24–25 point to “\n”, space, “(”, “-”, “No”, “1”, “...”, “ On”, “ in” — consistent with article/listicle and page-scaffold formatting.
- The difference is concentrated in late layers (big spikes from ~14 through 25), suggesting a change in output-style priors rather than base linguistic representations.

I cannot identify a more specific objective (e.g., summarization, RLHF safety, etc.) from this evidence; the clearest interpretable difference is a domain/style shift toward news/blog/web-page content and formatting.
